traceability.notes:
All explicit acceptance criteria and requirements in docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md are implemented and verified:
- Core Functionality: The `require-branch-annotation` rule detects missing @story/@req annotations across all significant branch types (if, loops, switch cases, try/catch), with comprehensive valid/invalid RuleTester cases. - Quality & Integration: The rule follows ESLint best practices (meta, schema, message IDs, separation of concerns into helpers) and handles nested and varied branch patterns. Configuration is validated via `validateBranchTypes`, which either returns a branchTypes array or a Program listener that reports invalid configuration. - User Experience: Errors use a clear, single message template `Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}.`, which, together with the node location and the specific `missing` value (@story or @req), clearly communicates what is wrong and why. Autofixes insert placeholder annotations where appropriate, aiding developer workflow. - Error Handling: Edge cases such as default switch cases (ignored via significance criteria), nested branches, missing-only-story vs missing-only-req, and invalid `branchTypes` values are explicitly tested and handled gracefully. - Documentation: A dedicated rule doc (docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md) ties back to this story, documents configuration and behavior, and includes correct/incorrect and invalid-configuration examples. - Definition of Done: The rule is integrated into plugin presets (recommended/strict), thoroughly tested (functional, helper-level, and performance tests), and documented. Performance tests confirm acceptable behavior on files with many nested branches.
Given the direct mapping between the story’s requirements (REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION, REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION, REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING, REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA, REQ-NESTED-HANDLING, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION) and the implemented code, tests, and docs, this story is fully implemented and passes.
